title: Juniper and the Portrait
premise: Edmund Quintana, a meticulous property surveyor, is sent to appraise Juniper Hall, a house that answers her measurements with measurements of its own. When every mirror begins reflecting the rooms one second late, she discovers the founders built the house as a ritual engine sustained by a found family of caretakers — and it is starving. To escape, Edmund must finish the ritual the founders abandoned, but completing it demands she surrender the person she loves most to the house's hunger. In the end she chooses a third path: she rewrites the survey, reclassifying the house as a grave rather than a home, and the mirrors finally reflect the present — at the cost of her ever being believed again.
about_author: Noor Joubert is the pen name of a former building inspector who spent a decade documenting structures that should not have stood. They write horror about paperwork, obligation, and the houses that keep accounts of their own.

chapters.title: The Commission
chapters.summary: Edmund Quintana accepts an appraisal of Juniper Hall, a derelict estate with no listed owner. POV Edmund. She arrives with instruments and habits, establishing her creed: documentation is a kind of prayer. Emotional beat: professional detachment masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Plumb and Level
chapters.summary: Edmund surveys the ground floor; her laser level returns readings that disagree with themselves, as if the house is taller inside than out. POV Edmund. She documents the anomaly and feels, for the first time in years, observed. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into fascination.

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Ledger
chapters.summary: In the study she finds a ledger of previous surveyors, each entry ending mid-sentence. The last name is her own, dated next week. POV Edmund, with a brief archival interlude in the ledger's voice. Emotional beat: dread dressed as curiosity.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: At dusk, every mirror in the house reflects each room a full second behind reality. Edmund tests it with a metronome, a match, her own hand. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: the cold certainty that the delay is widening.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Middle
chapters.summary: Standing between two facing mirrors, Edmund sees herself in the reflection before she moves — and then the reflection keeps moving without her. POV Edmund, briefly the reflection's. Emotional beat: the self becomes unreliable territory.

chapters.title: Juniper
chapters.summary: Edmund meets Juniper Reyes, the last caretaker's daughter, who has lived off-grid near the house her whole life. Juniper explains the founders built the Hall as a ritual engine that feeds on a household. POV Juniper. Emotional beat: wary alliance, the first warmth Edmund has felt in years.

chapters.title: What the Founders Started
chapters.summary: In the cellar, they find the founders' covenant: nine names, nine duties, a ritual meant to bind the house's hunger into something like love. The ninth line is blank. POV Juniper. Emotional beat: hope curdling into obligation.

chapters.title: Inventory of Rooms
chapters.summary: Edmund maps rooms that appear only in reflection — a nursery, a chapel, a corridor of doors. The house is offering her a larger home than any she has known. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: temptation; the house as suitor.

chapters.title: The Ninth Name
chapters.summary: Juniper reveals her family's duty: each generation supplies a name to the blank line. Her mother's name is there. Hers is expected next. POV Juniper. Emotional beat: resentment of inherited duty, and Edmund's fury on her behalf.

chapters.title: Appraised
chapters.summary: The house begins appraising Edmund back — her debts, her estranged sister, her hunger for belonging — in ledger entries that appear overnight in her own handwriting. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: exposure; the house knows what she'd trade.

chapters.title: The Founders' Descendants
chapters.summary: Three descendants arrive uninvited, polite and wrong, to 'assist with the closing.' They want the ritual finished on their terms, with Juniper's name. POV Juniper. Emotional beat: found family versus blood obligation.

chapters.title: Delay of Five Seconds
chapters.summary: The mirrors now lag five seconds. Edmund watches her own reflection live a life slightly ahead of hers — kinder, braver. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: grief for the self she might have been.

chapters.title: A Night in the Chapel of Reflection
chapters.summary: Trapped overnight in the reflected chapel, Edmund meets the accumulated reflections of past caretakers, who beg her to finish the ritual and free them. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: compassion weaponized.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: The descendants present the contract: finish the ritual, name Juniper, inherit the Hall. Edmund, tempted by the promise that the house could hold a family together forever, nearly signs. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: power's corruption wearing the face of love.

chapters.title: What Juniper Saw
chapters.summary: Juniper, spying on the meeting, believes Edmund considered trading her. She flees into the reflected wing of the house. POV Juniper. Emotional beat: betrayal, the fragile found family cracking.

chapters.title: The Reflected Wing
chapters.summary: Edmund goes in after her, navigating rooms that exist only one second behind, guided by the lag itself. The house tries to keep her by showing her the family she never had. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: love against duty, made literal.

chapters.title: The Blank Line
chapters.summary: Juniper is found at the covenant, pen in hand, ready to write her own name to end the starving. Edmund stops her — not with argument, but by writing her own survey over the page. POV both. Emotional beat: refusal of the ritual's terms.

chapters.title: Reclassification
chapters.summary: Edmund drafts a new appraisal declaring Juniper Hall a grave, not a dwelling — a structure owed mourning, not tenants. The house convulses; the mirrors lag a full minute. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: defiance as an act of care.

chapters.title: The House Answers
chapters.summary: The founders' descendants attempt to force the ritual at the climax; the house, offered a choice between hunger and grief, chooses grief. The reflected caretakers are released. POV Juniper. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into mourning.

chapters.title: Sunrise Appraisal
chapters.summary: Dawn. The mirrors reflect the present exactly. The Hall stands empty and honest, its ledger closed. Edmund signs her final survey; Juniper decides what to do with the land. POV both. Emotional beat: exhausted tenderness.

chapters.title: What Documentation Keeps
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Edmund's report is dismissed by her firm as fabrication; her reputation frays. But Juniper visits, and they plant a garden where the chapel stood. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: the found family survives the house.

chapters.title: The Last Reflection
chapters.summary: Final image: in a small mirror in Juniper's new cottage, the room reflects perfectly — except once, briefly, it shows two women planting, one second early, a future the house never got to keep. POV omniscient. Emotional beat: quiet, earned grace.
